note.headline: Rates rally, credit doesn't follow, and breadth stays negative under a flat tape
note.standfirst: The S&P added 0.17% while the curve fell 6 to 8bp across the belly and long end, and credit spreads did not confirm the move. Positioning into month end looks split between a rates market pricing relief and a credit market pricing caution.
takeaways: Treasuries rallied in a parallel shift of 6 to 8bp with 2s10s unchanged at 27bp, a duration bid rather than a curve trade.
Credit sold off across investment grade, high yield and EM sovereign even as equities held flat, a divergence the risk barometer flags directly.
Mega-cap chip and platform names carried the index while breadth was negative, 12 advancers against 13 decliners.
Bitcoin rose 6.48% and led every component of the risk score, well ahead of equities or credit.
note.desk_view:
The headline print says nothing happened. Under it, two markets told different stories. Rates rallied hard, the 10-year yield down 7bp to 4.94%, while MOVE rose 5.79% on the same day yields fell, which is not the calm-market signature. Credit sold off in the same session: investment grade (LQD) down 0.44%, high yield (HYG) down 0.24%, EM sovereign (EMB) down 0.30%, all printing near their lows for the period. When duration bids and credit offers at the same time, the market is pricing a slowdown, not a soft landing. That is the tension this note keeps returning to.

The level that decides it is the 10-year yield. A close back above 4.94% with credit still soft would confirm a growth scare repricing across the curve. A break lower in yields alongside a bid returning to HYG and LQD would say the rally is a genuine risk-off flight to quality that credit simply lagged. Right now credit is not participating in the rates rally, and that gap has to close one way or the other before the tape can trust either move.
watching: Whether HYG and LQD stabilize or extend losses alongside a rates market still bid.
The 10-year yield's reaction near 4.94%, the level that held on the day's low print.
Whether breadth turns positive if chip and platform leadership fades.
MOVE index direction, since a further rise alongside falling yields would mark a repricing of rate volatility, not just a rally.
note.equities:
The S&P 500 closed up 0.17% and the Nasdaq 100 added 0.67%, both carried by a narrow set of names. AVGO rose 2.97%, AMD rose 2.70%, NVDA rose 1.34%. The Dow fell 0.18% and the Russell 2000 fell 0.50%, and the S&P MidCap 400 and NYSE Composite both closed lower, confirming the rally was concentrated at the top of the index and did not extend to small or mid caps.

Breadth was negative, 12 advancers to 13 decliners with a dispersion reading of 1.52, and sector rotation showed the same split. Technology led at +0.82%, Industrials added 0.44%, but Materials fell 1.42%, Utilities fell 1.42%, Communications fell 1.37% and Consumer Staples fell 0.83%. NFLX led losses at -4.67%, META fell 2.43%, ORCL fell 1.98%. The market bought chips and sold defensives and communications in the same session, an unusual pairing that argues for stock-specific stories over a clean macro rotation.
note.rates:
The curve shifted down in parallel, 2-year yields fell 7bp to 4.67%, 5-year fell 8bp to 4.78%, 10-year fell 7bp to 4.94%, 30-year fell 6bp to 5.29%. 2s10s held flat at 27bp and 5s30s widened 2bp to 51bp, so the belly outperformed slightly on a small twist within an otherwise parallel move. 3-month 10-year fell 5bp to 82bp.

Breakevens were mixed: 5-year breakeven fell 1bp to 2.31%, 10-year breakeven held at 2.33%, and the 5y5y forward rose 1bp to 2.35%. 10-year TIPS real yields fell 7bp to 2.61%, so the rally in nominal yields was mostly a real rate move, not an inflation story. MOVE rose 5.79%, the largest single move in the volatility complex, and 7-10 year Treasuries (IEF) sit at one of the period's lows even as prices rallied on the day, a sign the rate move has not settled positioning.
note.credit: Every major credit proxy fell and several sit at period lows: US investment grade (LQD) fell 0.44% and is at a low for the period, US high yield (HYG) fell 0.24% and is also at a low, JNK fell 0.20%, EM sovereign USD (EMB) fell 0.30% and is at a low, and leveraged loans (BKLN) fell 0.10%. The tone is soft and broad rather than concentrated in one sleeve, and it stands in contrast to the rally in the underlying Treasury curve.
note.fx: The dollar index was flat, down 0.01%. EUR/USD rose 0.17% and GBP/USD rose 0.08%. USD/JPY rose 0.54%, sitting near the top of its range for the period alongside USD/CHF and USD/TRY, both flagged among the session's highs. AUD/USD rose 0.47%. In the EM bloc, USD/BRL fell 0.17%, USD/MXN fell 0.12% and USD/INR fell 0.28%, all dollar-negative moves, while USD/TRY pushed to a high for the period, the one clear outlier.
note.commodities: Crude fell sharply, WTI down 6.32% and Brent down 5.77%, the largest moves in the entire fact set. Gold rose 0.37% and silver rose 2.01%, both firm. Copper rose 1.96% and aluminium rose 0.81%, an industrial metals bid that sits awkwardly next to the crude sell-off. Agricultural markets were soft: coffee fell 4.60%, cocoa fell 7.66%, wheat fell 1.86%, soybeans fell 1.27%, while sugar rose 4.94%.
note.volatility: The VIX fell 4.08% and VIX 9-day fell 8.36%, both pricing calm in equities. But MOVE rose 5.79% and SKEW rose 1.65%, so the cost of tail protection in rates and in equity left-tail structures both went up on a day when the headline equity vol index went down. Protection against a rates shock or a large equity drawdown got more expensive even as at-the-money equity vol got cheaper.
note.digital: Digital assets outperformed every other asset class by a wide margin: Bitcoin rose 6.48%, Ether rose 7.57%, Solana rose 11.66% and XRP rose 8.23%. Bitcoin's contribution to the risk barometer was the largest of any component at 2.62, well above copper at 1.36 and USD/JPY at 1.23. The move looks like a beta-to-risk trade running well ahead of both equities and credit, not a move confirmed elsewhere in the risk complex.
note.international: European markets closed broadly higher: the EURO STOXX 50 rose 0.90%, the DAX rose 0.70%, the CAC rose 0.57%, the IBEX rose 1.00% and the FTSE MIB rose 0.80%. The FTSE 100 was the exception, down 1.45%. Asia was mixed: the Nikkei rose 0.33% and the TAIEX rose 0.96%, while the Hang Seng fell 0.44% and the KOSPI and SENSEX were both roughly flat. The handoff to New York was a firm European session and a directionless Asian one, neither of which anticipated the size of the rates move or the crude sell-off that followed.
note.correlation:
The session broke the usual link between rates and credit. Treasuries rallied on falling yields while every credit proxy sold off, a combination that normally moves together during a flight to quality and normally moves apart only when credit-specific stress is building. The risk barometer detail confirms it directly: LQD, MOVE, HYG and EMB were the four most negative contributions to the score while USD/JPY, copper and Bitcoin were the most positive, so risk appetite and safe-haven demand both registered as elevated in the same reading, which they cannot both be true.

If that gap closes through credit catching up and reversing higher, it would confirm the rates rally as a straightforward growth scare that credit simply lagged by a session. If it closes through rates giving back today's move while credit stays soft, that says the rates rally was a false signal and credit had the direction right. Either resolution matters more than today's index closes, which were both quiet enough to hide the split underneath.
